title: 第三十章 金声
content_zh:
东岭碎石坡下的石缝，成了陈默新的、更加隐秘也更加孤寂的“巢穴”。

    此地距离杂役院已有小半个时辰的山路，位于东岭砍柴区域的边缘，平日里除了像陈默这样深入此片区域砍柴的杂役，少有人至。碎石坡是多年前一次山体滑坡的产物，大大小小的灰褐色石块堆积成一道缓坡，上面攀爬着顽强的藤蔓和稀疏的灌木。石缝入口被几块崩落的、半人高的巨岩和茂密的、带刺的“金刚藤”几乎完全遮掩，若非陈默之前偶然追兔至此，绝难发现。

    入口仅容一人侧身挤入，向内曲折丈许，豁然开朗，形成一个约莫丈许方圆、高及人腰的不规则天然石穴。穴顶是倾斜的岩壁，有数道狭窄的裂缝，白日可透下些许天光，夜晚则完全漆黑。穴内干燥，铺着一层厚厚的、不知积攒了多少年的、干燥的枯叶和尘土，散发着陈腐的泥土和草木气息。最深处，还有一小块相对平整、略显光滑的青石，似乎是天然形成，正好可以用来放置东西。

    此地虽阴冷潮湿，寒气比杂役院更重，但胜在绝对隐蔽，且远离人烟。陈默在首次转移物资、确认安全的深夜，便喜欢上了这里。至少，在这里，他无需时刻紧绷神经，担心下一刻就有人从阴影中走出。

    转移的过程有惊无险。他抱着沉重的包裹，在黑暗山林中潜行，如同背负着整个世界的秘密。夜枭的啼叫，风吹林梢的呜咽，甚至自己踩断枯枝的轻微声响，都让他心惊肉跳。左胸伤处和膻中穴的隐痛，在疾行和紧张下变得更加清晰。但他咬着牙，凭借着对山路的熟悉和一股近乎偏执的谨慎，终于安全抵达，并将包裹藏进了石穴最深处，用枯叶和碎石做了伪装。

    接下来的日子，他的生活轨迹变得更加固定，也更为分裂。

    白日，他依旧是杂役院里那个沉默、迟缓、病弱、似乎随时会倒下、也无人关心的影子。砍柴、挑水、清理，完成所有指派的话计，动作机械，眼神空洞，完美地融入那片麻木的背景之中。他不再尝试在劳作中融入任何修炼的韵律，也不再刻意观察周围的目光和议论，仿佛真的已经“认命”，成了一具被抽去灵魂、只知道重复劳作的空壳。只有当偶尔无人注意的间隙，他才会用眼角余光，飞快地扫过山林深处，那个藏着秘密的方向，眼神深处，掠过一丝极其微弱的、与外表截然不同的锐光。

    夜晚，当杂役院彻底沉入鼾声和黑暗，他便会如幽灵般起身，带上柴刀，悄无声息地溜出侧门，没入山林，向着东岭碎石坡疾行。夜晚的山林更加危险，但也更加“安全”——至少，来自“人”的威胁暂时远去，只需提防可能出现的野兽和自身行迹的暴露。他走得很快，很轻，体内那缕微弱的水木气息，在奔跑中被调动起来，不是为了提速，而是为了让他与周围山林的气息更加“贴合”，脚步声、呼吸声、甚至衣袂摩擦声，都降到最低。

    抵达石穴，他并不立刻开始“工作”。而是会先盘膝坐在那块青石上，就着岩缝透下的、极其微弱的星光或远处主峰投来的、疏离的灯火，运转苏芸所授的行气法。在石穴这种更加“天然”、远离杂役院污浊气息的环境中，行气法似乎运转得比在杂役院时顺畅了一丝。虽然灵气依旧稀薄驳杂，难以引动，但至少心神更容易沉静，体内那缕气息的流转，对膻中穴“缝隙”和周身经脉的温养，似乎也更有效一分。运行一个周天，平复因疾行而略微急促的气息和心跳，也驱散一些石穴中的阴寒。

    然后，他才点亮那盏极其简陋的、用破陶碗和一点点偷藏下来的灯油、棉线制成的、豆大灯苗的“油灯”。昏黄、摇曳、随时可能熄灭的光晕，勉强照亮方寸之地，也映亮了他沉静专注的脸庞。

    “工作”继续。清理工具上的锈迹。

    有了之前的经验和教训，他更加谨慎，也更加“奢侈”地使用着那些来之不易的“材料”。酸浆草汁液、乌柏叶水、明矾粉末，被他小心地调配、试验，寻找着最适合当前锈蚀程度的配比。清理的动作，也更加轻柔、耐心，如同在剥离蝴蝶翅膀上最细微的粉尘。他不再追求速度，只求稳妥，宁愿慢一些，也不能再损伤这些来之不易的工具。

    那件弧形薄片工具，率先被完全清理出来。全长约七寸，宽约两指，通体呈现一种深沉的、近乎墨黑的青灰色，表面布满了细微的锻打纹理和岁月留下的氧化斑点，并不光亮，却自有一种沉厚、内敛的质感。最让陈默惊讶的是其刃口。在清除了表面的锈垢和氧化物后，那薄如蝉翼的刃口，竟依然保留着极其微弱的、几乎难以察觉的锋锐！虽然远未达到“吹毛断发”的程度，但用手指指腹极其小心地横向拂过，能清晰地感觉到一种清晰、凝练、带着细微“阻力”的锐利感，与普通柴刀的“锋利”截然不同，更像是一种被“淬炼”到极致的、属于金属本身的“锋芒”。

    这刃口，显然不是用来砍劈的，更像是一种用于精细刮削、切割的“刃”。

    陈默尝试着，用这薄片的刃口，去轻轻刮擦那块黑铁碎片。这一次，不再是“刮”，而是一种极其轻微的、带着角度的“削”。只听“嘶”的一声极轻微的、如同裂帛的声响，黑铁碎片表面，竟真的被“削”下了一层比头发丝还要细薄、闪烁着幽暗金属光泽的薄片！这薄片比之前用黑铁碎片互刮或钩子刮擦得到的粉末，更加均匀、细腻，质地似乎也更为“纯粹”！

    成功了！这薄片工具，果然是专门用于处理这种坚硬金属的“削刀”！其本身的材质和特殊的刃口处理，使其能够以最小的力量，对黑纹铁进行精细的“切削”！

    陈默压抑着心中的激动，小心地将那削下的金属薄片收集到一片洗净的、光滑的石片上。薄片在油灯下泛着幽暗的、近乎蓝色的冷光，边缘呈现出一种极其细微的、类似贝壳断口的层叠纹理，美丽而神秘。

    他再接再厉，又用这薄片，尝试处理那件弯钩工具上最难清理的、靠近钩柄连接处的一圈顽固锈蚀。薄片刃口以极小的角度切入锈层与金属本体的缝隙，轻轻一挑，竟将那圈结合紧密的锈蚀，如同剥开干涸的泥皮般，整块剥离下来！露出了底下完好无损的、颜色比薄片工具稍浅、带着一种暗哑青灰色的金属。这弯钩工具的材质，似乎与薄片又略有不同，更显“韧”性。

    弯钩工具最终也被完全清理出来。长约一尺，通体笔直，唯最前端弯出一个精巧而锐利的钩尖。钩身截面呈不规则的六边形，布满细密的螺旋锻纹，显然经过特殊的折叠锻打。钩尖异常尖锐，在油灯下泛着一点幽冷的寒芒，虽经岁月锈蚀，那份穿透力和“咬合”感，依旧透过视觉传递出来。陈默尝试用钩尖，轻轻“点”在黑铁碎片上，几乎不需要用力，钩尖便轻松地“钉”了进去，留下一个清晰而深邃的小点。这绝非普通的“钩”，更像是一种用于“刺探”、“开孔”或“勾取”精细物件的“探针”或“锥”。

    最后是那件凿杆。清理耗时最久，因为其锈蚀最为严重，且杆身较长，结构相对简单，但锈层与本体几乎融为一体。陈默花费了数个夜晚，用尽了耐心和调配的“药水”，才终于将其清理出原貌。这是一根长约尺半、拇指粗细的实心金属杆，一头被打磨成扁平如凿的楔形，边缘厚实，显然用于承受敲击；另一头则是浑圆的柱形，便于握持。通体颜色与弯钩相似，呈暗哑青灰色，但质地感觉更加“敦实”、“厚重”，充满了力量感。这是一件纯粹的“力”的工具，用于“凿”、“击”、“撬”。

    三件工具，终于以它们完整的面貌，呈现在陈默面前。虽然依旧布满岁月的痕迹，黯淡无光，但那份属于精良工具特有的、功能明确的“气质”，已然透过粗糙的表面散发出来。它们沉默地躺在青石上，在豆大的灯苗映照下，仿佛三头从漫长沉眠中苏醒、收敛了所有爪牙、却依旧散发着危险气息的古老金属兽。

    陈默的目光，在三件工具和旁边那几块沉甸甸的黑纹铁锭之间，缓缓移动。一个清晰而完整的“链条”，在他脑海中逐渐成形。

    削刀（薄片），用于精细切削、获取均匀材料。

    探针（弯钩），用于刺探、定位、开孔、勾取。

    凿杆，用于大力凿击、开槽、破碎。

    而黑纹铁锭，便是需要被处理的“材料”。

    这套工具，显然是一整套用于初步加工、处理“黑纹铁”这类特殊坚硬金属的专用工具！虽然简陋，但功能齐全，设计合理，绝非寻常铁匠铺的产物。留书之人所谓“提炼不易”，恐怕不仅仅是指采矿和熔炼，也包括了后续这种精细的初步加工。

    现在，工具在手，材料在侧。他，能做什么？
content_en:
The crevices under the gravel slope of Dongling have become Chen Mo's new, more secret and lonely "nest".
This place is half an hour away from the handyman's yard on a mountain road, and is located on the edge of the Dongling firewood cutting area. On weekdays, except for handymen like Chen Mo who go deep into this area to cut firewood, few people come here.The gravel slope is the product of a landslide many years ago. Large and small gray-brown stones are piled up into a gentle slope, with tenacious vines and sparse shrubs climbing on it.The entrance to the stone crevice was almost completely obscured by several crumbling giant rocks half as tall as a man and dense, thorny "King Kong vines". It would have been difficult to find it if Chen Mo hadn't accidentally chased a rabbit here before.
The entrance allows only one person to squeeze in sideways, and then twists and turns inward about ten feet, and suddenly opens up, forming an irregular natural stone cave about ten feet in diameter and as high as a person's waist.The top of the cave is a sloping rock wall with several narrow cracks. A little light can shine through during the day, but it is completely dark at night.The inside of the cave is dry, covered with a thick layer of dry leaves and dust accumulated over many years, exuding the smell of stale earth and vegetation.In the deepest part, there is a small piece of relatively flat and slightly smooth bluestone, which seems to be naturally formed and can be used to place things.
Although this place is cold and humid, and the air is more chilly than the courtyard, the advantage is that it is absolutely hidden and far away from human habitation.Chen Mo fell in love with this place late at night when he first transferred supplies and confirmed safety.At least, here, he didn't have to worry about someone walking out of the shadows at the next moment.
The transfer process was uneventful.Holding the heavy package, he sneaked through the dark mountains and forests, as if he was carrying the secrets of the entire world.The cry of the night owl, the whimpering of the treetops in the wind, and even the slight sound of breaking dead branches when he stepped on them all made him tremble with fear.The dull pain in the left chest injury and Tanzhong point became clearer under the rapid movement and tension.But he gritted his teeth, relied on his familiarity with the mountain roads and an almost paranoid caution, and finally arrived safely, and hid the package in the deepest part of the cave, disguised with dead leaves and gravel.
In the following days, his life trajectory became more fixed and more divided.
During the day, he was still the silent, slow, sickly figure in the yard, who seemed to be falling at any time and no one cared about him.Chopping wood, fetching water, cleaning, completing all assigned tasks, with mechanical movements and empty eyes, perfectly blending into the numb background.He no longer tries to incorporate any cultivation rhythm into his work, and he no longer deliberately observes the gazes and comments around him. It seems as if he has truly "accepted his fate" and become an empty shell with his soul removed and only knows how to work repeatedly.Only when no one was paying attention, he would use the corner of his eye to quickly scan the depths of the mountain forest, the direction where the secret was hidden. Deep in his eyes, an extremely weak and sharp light that was completely different from the appearance passed through.
At night, when the yard was completely enveloped in snoring and darkness, he would get up like a ghost, take a hatchet, quietly slip out of the side door, disappear into the forest, and rush towards the gravel slope of Dongling.The mountain forest at night is more dangerous, but it is also "safer" - at least, the threat from "people" is temporarily gone, and you only need to be careful of possible wild beasts and the exposure of your own whereabouts.He walked very fast and very lightly, and the faint breath of water and wood in his body was mobilized during the run, not to speed up, but to make him more "fit" with the breath of the surrounding mountains and forests. The sound of footsteps, breathing, and even the friction of clothes were all reduced to a minimum.
Arriving at the cave, he did not immediately start "working".Instead, he would first sit cross-legged on the bluestone, and use the extremely weak starlight coming from the cracks in the rock or the distant lights cast from the main peak in the distance to practice the Qi movement method taught by Su Yun.In a more "natural" environment like a stone cave, far away from the dirty atmosphere of the courtyard, the qi movement method seems to run a little more smoothly than in the courtyard.Although the spiritual energy is still thin and mixed, and difficult to induce, at least the mind is easier to calm down, and the flow of breath in the body seems to be more effective in warming and nourishing the "gap" of the Tanzhong point and the meridians around the body.Running for a week will calm down the slightly rapid breathing and heartbeat caused by fast walking, and also dispel the coldness in some stone caves.
Then, he lit the extremely simple "oil lamp" made of a broken pottery bowl and a little hidden lamp oil and cotton thread, with a large sprout.The dim, swaying halo, which could go out at any time, barely illuminated a small area, and also illuminated his calm and focused face.
The "work" continues.Clean rust from tools.
With his previous experiences and lessons, he became more cautious and used those hard-earned "materials" more "lavishly".He carefully mixed and tested the physalis juice, cypress leaf water, and alum powder to find the most suitable ratio for the current degree of rust.The cleaning action is also more gentle and patient, like peeling off the finest dust from a butterfly's wings.He no longer pursues speed, only stability. He would rather go slower than damage these hard-won tools.
The curved sheet tool was the first to be completely cleaned out.It is about seven inches in length and about two fingers wide. The whole body is a deep, almost blackish blue-gray. The surface is covered with subtle forging textures and oxidized spots left by the years. It is not shiny, but has a thick and restrained texture.What surprised Chen Mo the most was its blade.After removing the rust and oxides on the surface, the thin edge still retains an extremely weak, almost imperceptible sharpness!Although it is far from the level of "blowing hair and breaking hair", if you use your fingertips to brush it horizontally very carefully, you can clearly feel a clear, concise, sharp feeling with subtle "resistance", which is completely different from the "sharpness" of an ordinary hatchet. It is more like an "edge" that has been "tempered" to the extreme and belongs to the metal itself.
This blade is obviously not used for chopping, but more like a "blade" used for fine scraping and cutting.
Chen Mo tried to use the cutting edge of this thin piece to gently scratch the piece of black iron.This time, it is no longer "scraping", but an extremely slight, angular "shaving".There was only a slight "hissing" sound, like cracking silk, and a layer of thin flakes thinner than a hair, shining with a dark metallic luster, was actually "shaving" off the surface of the black iron fragments!This flake is more uniform and finer than the powder obtained by scraping each other with black iron fragments or scratching with a hook, and the texture seems to be more "pure"!
Success!This thin tool is indeed a "sharpening knife" specially designed to handle such hard metal!Its own material and special edge treatment enable it to perform fine "cutting" on black grained iron with minimal force!
Chen Mo suppressed the excitement in his heart and carefully collected the shaved metal flakes onto a clean, smooth stone.The thin slices glowed with a dark, almost blue cold light under the oil lamp, and the edges showed an extremely fine layered texture that resembled the fracture of a shell, which was beautiful and mysterious.
He continued his efforts and used this thin slice again to try to deal with the most difficult area of ​​the hook tool to clean, a ring of stubborn rust near the hook handle connection.The cutting edge of the thin blade cut into the gap between the rust layer and the metal body at a very small angle, and with a gentle lift, the tightly bound ring of rust was peeled off in one piece, just like peeling off dried mud!The metal underneath was intact, slightly lighter in color than the flake tool, and with a dull bluish-gray color.The material of this hook tool seems to be slightly different from the thin film, and it is more "tough".
The hook tool was eventually completely cleaned out as well.It is about a foot long and straight, except for a delicate and sharp hook point curved at the front end.The hook body has an irregular hexagonal cross-section and is covered with fine spiral forging patterns. It has obviously been specially folded and forged.The tip of the hook is extremely sharp and glows with a cold light under the oil lamp. Although it has been rusted by years, the penetrating power and "biting" feeling are still conveyed through the eyes.Chen Mo tried to use the tip of the hook to lightly "click" on the black iron fragment. With almost no effort, the tip of the hook easily "nailed" in, leaving a clear and deep small spot.This is by no means an ordinary "hook", but more like a "probe" or "cone" used to "probe", "open holes" or "hook" delicate objects.
Finally, there’s the chisel piece.Cleaning takes the longest time because the rust is the most severe, the shaft is long, and the structure is relatively simple, but the rust layer is almost integrated with the body.Chen Mo spent several nights, exhausted his patience and prepared "potions" before finally cleaning it up to its original appearance.This is a solid metal rod about a foot and a half long and about the thickness of a thumb. One end is polished into a flat wedge shape with a thick edge, obviously used to withstand knocks; the other end is rounded and cylindrical for easy holding.The color of the whole body is similar to that of the hook, which is dull blue-gray, but the texture feels more "solid" and "thick", full of a sense of strength.This is a tool of pure "power", used for "chiseling", "hitting" and "prying".
The three tools finally appeared in front of Chen Mo in their complete appearance.Although it is still full of traces of time and dull, the "temperament" with clear functions unique to fine tools has already been radiated through the rough surface.They lay silently on the bluestone. Under the illumination of the big lamps, they looked like three ancient metal beasts that had awakened from a long slumber and restrained all their claws, but still exuded a dangerous aura.
Chen Mo's eyes moved slowly between the three tools and the heavy black-grained iron ingots next to them.A clear and complete "chain" gradually took shape in his mind.
Sharpener (thin slice) for fine cutting and obtaining uniform material.
Probe (hook), used for probing, positioning, opening holes, and hooking.
Chisel rod, used for vigorous chiseling, grooving, and crushing.
The black-grained iron ingots are the "materials" that need to be processed.
This set of tools is obviously a set of special tools used for preliminary processing and processing of special hard metals such as "black grained iron"!Although simple, it has complete functions and reasonable design. It is definitely not the product of an ordinary blacksmith shop.What the person who left the letter said "refining is not easy" probably refers not only to mining and smelting, but also to the subsequent fine preliminary processing.
Now, the tools are in hand and the materials are at your side.What can he do?
